name: EIA Open Data API v2
summary: US Energy Information Administration data on electricity, oil, natural gas, coal, nuclear, emissions and forecasts, with a free API key.
description: A hierarchical REST API: the root lists routes such as electricity, natural-gas, petroleum, coal, nuclear-outages, co2-emissions, seds, steo (Short-Term Energy Outlook), aeo and ieo (outlooks) and international. Each route exposes facets, frequencies and data columns, and a /data endpoint returns the rows. Data can be filtered by facet, period range and sorted.

auth.notes: Free key by email registration. A request without a key returns 403 API_KEY_MISSING. The shared key DEMO_KEY was accepted on the day of verification but is not mentioned on the docs pages fetched, so treat it as unreliable for production.

rate_limit.summary: Not documented on the pages fetched. DEMO_KEY responses carried x-ratelimit-limit: 10 (period not stated).

endpoints.summary: Describe a route: child routes, facets, frequencies and data columns

license.name: US Government data; EIA states it is provided free of charge

coverage.geographic: United States (states, regions, plants) plus international energy statistics
coverage.temporal: Varies by route; monthly and annual series, some going back decades, plus forecasts

agent_notes: Walk the route tree first: GET /v2/electricity/retail-sales/ lists the facets and data columns you must name in data[0]=... . Numbers come back as strings. JSON is capped at 5000 rows per call; page with offset and length, and constrain with start/end and facets. Query parameters use bracket syntax, so URL-encode the brackets.
caveats: Without a key the API answers HTTP 403 with code API_KEY_MISSING.
Too-large requests return a warning (incomplete return) in the body, still with HTTP 200.
Values are strings, and units are in a separate field such as price-units.

verification.notes: Exact example executed with the shared DEMO_KEY; the same request without a key returned 403 API_KEY_MISSING.
